claims.text: OutboxRelay sets each published message's MessageId to the outbox row's id, so every copy of one outbox row carries the same message id; different outbox rows (different events, even for one order) carry different ids.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Messaging/RabbitMqPublisher.cs:26 (MessageId = message.Id), called only by OutboxRelay.RelayDueAsync; DonHang.Tests/Messaging/OutboxRelayTests.cs:38

claims.text: Messages repeat two ways at stage-3: the relay republishes a row if it stops after RabbitMQ's confirm and before its commit; RabbitMQ redelivers if the channel closes after the save and before the ack. Recording published_at first, or acking first, would lose the message on a stop in between.
claims.source_hint: prereqs backend.l3.outbox-relay, backend.l3.consumer-acknowledgements; RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms > Automatic Requeueing

claims.text: HandleAsync takes a NotificationsDbContext from a new scope (lines 100-101), adds an InboxMessage (102) and a notifications row (103), calls SaveChangesAsync once (106); catches only DbUpdateException where Inbox.IsDuplicate is true (109), logs, returns normally.

EF Core: by default, when the provider supports transactions, all changes in a single SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync call are applied in one transaction; if any command fails, the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Saving Data > Transactions > Default transaction behavior

claims.text: PostgreSQL refuses a row whose primary key or unique index value already exists (unique violation, SQLSTATE 23505), and the error aborts the enclosing transaction.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: 5.5 Constraints > Primary Keys / Unique Constraints; Appendix A PostgreSQL Error Codes (23505 unique_violation)

claims.text: Inbox.IsDuplicate (DonHang.Messaging/Inbox.cs, outside the excerpt) returns true when the inner exception is a PostgresException with SqlState unique violation on constraint PK_inbox_messages.

Any exception from HandleAsync other than the caught duplicate reaches OnReceivedAsync and the message is not acknowledged; when HandleAsync returns normally, OnReceivedAsync acknowledges the delivery.

NotificationsDbContext maps InboxMessage to table inbox_messages with MessageId as primary key (column message_id) and HandledAt as handled_at, in donhang_notifications, the same database as notifications.
RabbitMQ does not deduplicate messages by message id when routing or queueing them to classic or quorum queues: two publishes yield two messages, and a requeued message is delivered again.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Reliability Guide > Consumers (duplicates); Consumer Acknowledgements > redelivered flag; Publishers > message_id property

claims.text: SubjectFor in OrderEventsConsumer.cs maps six routing keys to email subjects: order.placed, order.cancelled, order.shipped, order.refund-requested, order.refunded, order.refund-failed.
OrderEventsConsumer does not send emails; it saves pending rows that NotificationSender sends, and NotificationSender sends first and records sent afterwards (at-least-once).

duplicate-message.sh publishes one order.shipped message for order 2 twice with one message id via the management API (printing routed: true/false), waits 2 s, lists notifications rows created since the start (order_id | subject) and counts inbox_messages rows with that id.
Expected output of duplicate-message.sh on a running stage-3 lab: two 'routed: true' lines, one row '2 | order shipped', and the count 1.
Keeping the inbox inside the same database as the effect is preferable when exactly-once effects are needed, because a record in another system (e.g. Redis) cannot commit atomically with the effect.
claims.source_hint: outline item 5; Reliability Guide (RabbitMQ) > idempotent consumers
